chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Hamzah ibn Ahmad, from Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him, or someone else asked him, about the bathhouse. He said: "Enter it wearing a waist-wrapper, lower your gaze, and do not wash from the well in which the bathhouse water gathers, for into it flows that with which the junub, the child of zina, and the nasibi hostile to us Ahl al-Bayt wash, and he is the worst of them."

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: one who shows hostility toward Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well or water-source where the bathhouse water gathers
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.بِمِئْزَرٍ: with a waist-wrapper covering the body
key_terms.غُضَّ بَصَرَكَ: lower your gaze and avoid looking at what is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What are the etiquettes and rulings for entering the bathhouse in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out etiquette and rulings related to entering the bathhouse, including covering oneself, lowering the gaze, and avoiding water that has collected from communal use. It reflects concerns of taharah (ritual purity) and proper conduct, while also strongly condemning the nasibi who is hostile to Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
